profile.address: 1111, Olive Street, Downtown, Saint Louis, Missouri, 63101
profile.reading:
This TierPoint facility is located in Saint Louis, Missouri, TierPoint's own corporate headquarters market, where the company operates three separate named data centers rather than one. Millpark, at 2315 Millpark Drive in suburban Maryland Heights, is the smallest of the three at more than 23,000 total square feet. Olive, at 1111 Olive Street in downtown St. Louis, spans more than 124,000 total square feet with an N+1 power design and 10 gigabit wave interconnection to other regional TierPoint sites. Locust, at 2300 Locust Street also in downtown St. Louis, is the newest and most significant of the three: TierPoint acquired the building outright on August 13, 2024, with a planned total investment of up to 150 million dollars, and CEO Jerry Kent described it as a direct response to strong demand for data center and AI GPU workload capacity, with the completed facility expected to become TierPoint's second largest data center company wide by critical load capacity, supporting roughly 80 construction jobs and 9 permanent positions.

Because this single map record cannot be confidently matched to one specific building among TierPoint's three St. Louis area facilities, all three are documented here rather than guessing which one this record represents. The Olive Street facility's power infrastructure includes N+1 configured 2,000 kilowatt Caterpillar diesel generators, providing roughly 4 megawatts of standby generation capacity, and its 10 gigabit wave connections give tenants low latency links to TierPoint's other regional sites without needing separate carrier circuits for site to site connectivity. Millpark, the smallest and longest established of the three St. Louis facilities, continues to serve customers with smaller footprint requirements and disaster recovery needs within the same metro area, while Locust represents TierPoint's newest investment in the market and its planned flagship for AI and GPU-driven capacity demand going forward.

All three facilities carry TierPoint's standard SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II, including HITRUST, compliance, along with HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GLBA, and ISO 27001 certification. TierPoint, headquartered in St. Louis, was formed in 2010 and has grown over more than a decade through a combination of new construction and the acquisition of established regional colocation providers, bringing operators serving distinct local markets together under a single national brand while preserving existing customer relationships in each market. The company now operates roughly 40 data centers across 20 US markets. As is standard industry practice, tenant identities are not publicly disclosed.

reading.body:
This TierPoint facility in downtown St. Louis publishes 11,000 square feet of production data center space and 4 megawatts of standby diesel generation capacity, but does not publish its IT load or supported accelerator count. The facility carries N+1 configured generators and 10 gigabit wave interconnection to other regional TierPoint sites, meaning tenants can route traffic between St. Louis facilities without external carrier circuits. The standby generation figure does not indicate sustained power supply to the data center and should not be read as colocation capacity.

The facility is certified for workloads subject to SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II audit, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GLBA, NIST SP 800-53, ISO 27001, ITAR, and EU-US Privacy Shield compliance. These certifications qualify the campus to host regulated healthcare, payment processing, government contracting, and national security workloads. No published data on Missouri's total data center capacity exists for this site to be ranked against, as Missouri has 8 mapped facilities but none publish power figures in the operator spec pages this site has read.

TierPoint operates three separate named facilities in the St. Louis area, of which this record describes the Olive Street location, the longest established. The operator's published reading indicates that TierPoint has separately acquired and is developing the Locust Street building as a flagship for AI and GPU capacity, describing it as planned to become the company's second largest facility by critical load and funded by a 150 million dollar investment, though Locust's specifications are not published. This facility's capacity is not documented.
